__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: Prometheus instance scraping declaragent /metrics (the CLI's 127.0.0.1:9464 listener, or the OTel-collector Prometheus exporter).

__layout_sketch__: │ │ restart │ circuit │ open 5m │ drain p99 (ms)   │ rate-limited (rate)  │   │
│ │ backlog │ paused  │ batch int ms │ batch rows   │ export failures   │     │
│ │ provider waits/s  │ tool waits/s      │ source DLQ/s │ source inflight│   │
All panels filter on `$server_id` / `$agent` / `$source` template variables.
Time range default 15m, refresh 30s — tuned for incident triage, not capacity planning.
description: Declaragent fleet dashboard — MCP health, audit / SIEM export back-pressure, rate limits, and dispatch DLQ flow. Scrapes the Prometheus endpoint exposed by `declaragent up -d` on 127.0.0.1:9464 (see docs/grafana/README.md). Ships with 0.7.6.

panels.title: MCP restarts (total)
panels.description: Sum of `mcp_server_restarts_total` across selected servers. Non-zero in steady state is a red flag — the supervisor is respawning. Drill into the per-server timeseries below when this climbs.

panels.title: Circuit state (max over servers)
panels.description: `mcp_server_circuit_state`: 0=closed (healthy), 1=half-open (probing), 2=open (shorting). Any value ≥ 1 means at least one supervised MCP server is degraded. Alert on `max(mcp_server_circuit_state) >= 2 for 1m`.

panels.title: Circuit-open transitions (5m increase)
panels.description: `increase(mcp_server_circuit_open_total[5m])`. Alert rule: `> 0` pages the MCP on-call — a circuit that just opened means users are now seeing tool-call failures. Suggested Alertmanager: `expr: increase(mcp_server_circuit_open_total[5m]) > 0`, `for: 0m`, severity page.

panels.title: Drain duration p99 (ms)
panels.description: `histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(mcp_server_drain_duration_ms_bucket[5m]))`. `outcome="timeout"` samples at the drain cap (default 2000ms) mean the supervisor gave up waiting for in-flight tool calls. Alert when p99 approaches the cap, e.g. `> 1500` for 5m.

panels.title: MCP rate-limit rejections (rps)
panels.description: `rate(mcp_server_rate_limited_total[1m])` — tool calls rejected by the aggregate per-server cap (Sprint 5 #27). Healthy fleet sits at 0. Persistent > 0 means either (a) the cap is too low or (b) a skill is hot-looping tool calls. Alert: `> 0.1` for 10m.

panels.title: Audit backlog (ms)
panels.description: `declaragent_audit_backpressure_backlog_ms` — age in ms of the oldest audit row not yet shipped to the SIEM exporter. The closest proxy to `audit_export_queue_depth` the runtime exposes. Alert when it grows past your SIEM's SLA (e.g. `> 60000` = 1 minute behind).

panels.title: Back-pressure active
panels.description: `declaragent_audit_backpressure_active` (gauge, 0|1). When 1, the audit-intake gate is engaged — new audit writes pause or drop per policy (Sprint 4 #11). Companion counter `declaragent_audit_backpressure_paused_total` counts activations.

panels.title: Batch interval (ms, adaptive)
panels.description: `declaragent_audit_batch_interval_ms` — current exporter tick cadence (Sprint 4 #12). The adaptive loop shortens when batches are full and lengthens when they're empty. A flat line pinned at `maxIntervalMs` means the exporter is idle; pinned at `minIntervalMs` means it's chasing a growing backlog.

panels.title: Batch rows (p50 / p95)
panels.description: `declaragent_audit_batch_rows_bucket` — rows per export tick. When p95 hugs `targetBatchRows` the adaptive loop is parked at steady state; when p95 >> target the exporter is behind.

panels.title: Export acked vs failures (rps)
panels.description: `rate(declaragent_audit_export_acked_total[1m])` vs `rate(declaragent_audit_export_failures_total[1m])`. Alert: failures > 0 sustained for 5m, or acked rate drops while `source_messages_processed` is rising.

panels.title: Exporter last_seq (catch-up tracer)
panels.description: `declaragent_audit_export_last_seq` — highest audit seq the SIEM exporter has ack'd. The slope should track the audit-write rate; a flat line means the exporter is stuck. Use this alongside the backlog_ms panel for a 2D picture of export health.

panels.title: Provider rate-limit waits (rps)
panels.description: `rate(declaragent_provider_rate_limit_waits[1m])` — how often the LLM-provider token bucket forced a call to wait (Anthropic 50rps / OpenRouter 20rps / default 10rps). Persistent non-zero = you're at quota. Pair with `declaragent_provider_rate_limit_wait_ms` p99 for impact.

panels.title: Tool rate-limit waits (rps)
panels.description: `rate(declaragent_tool_rate_limit_waits_total[1m])` per `agent` + `tool`. A persistent spike for one tool typically means the skill's loop needs throttling or the per-tool budget is too tight.

panels.title: Source DLQ rate (msg/s)
panels.description: `rate(source_messages_dlq[1m])` — messages that exhausted their retry budget and hit the dispatch DLQ (SQLite `rejected_events`). Non-zero is always a regression. Cross-reference with `declaragent events list --state circuit-open` and `declaragent dlq list --kind dispatch`.

panels.title: Source throughput + inflight
panels.description: `rate(source_messages_received[1m])` vs `rate(source_messages_processed[1m])`. Healthy source: processed ≈ received. A persistent gap means handler work is blocking or the normalizer is dropping messages.

panels.title: Source inflight handlers
panels.description: `source_inflight` — in-flight handler gauge, bounded above by the adapter's `limits.concurrency`. Persistent saturation at the cap means downstream latency is higher than configured throughput.

title: Declaragent fleet — MCP / audit / rate-limit / dispatch
